item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Another newbie here, working my way through the SCP articles numerically. This one is fantastic, not just for the content, which is one of my favorite compulsion-based ideas so far, but because of how the Foundation's portrayed. The focus on the medical procedures in the earlier scripts is very practical, and reminds the audience that the Foundation isn't just a scary underground lab that feeds criminals to monsters. And even in the Script 82, with Foundation operatives protecting the targeted individuals with lethal force, I think I can solidly say this is one of the times when the Foundation can justly come off as heroic, saving everyone they can from a seemingly eternal threat. Way to fucking go!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
We probably can't really predict the frequency of these things. Cult events may have been less frequent back then, but also consider that people's natural reaction to the script would prevent it from triggering. You'd probably run if everyone around you started chanting in eerie unison in Latin.

EDIT: To clarify, we could experiment with different buildings to find one that produces the Plurality Cult less often. But we don't know what would do that, and we don't know that some even more dangerous script wouldn't appear. If we just keep trying new and different structures, this raises the problem that the SCP continues anyhow during the renovations process, even if just in the streets. And it would be extremely hard to contain then, since it would no longer be conveniently be bounded by walls. In return for maybe making containment a bit easier in the future, we'd be letting a Euclid class be almost uncontained for months on end.
